facts.text: Boston earned its name from Major Thomas M., a 19th‑century figure honored when the town was incorporated in 1870.
In 1860 the town moved to sit beside the new Atlantic and Gulf Railroad, turning Boston into a regional shipping hub.
Boston’s 1913 Carnegie Library, one of Georgia’s few still operating libraries, remains a living testament to the town’s early philanthropy.
A 1969 federal lawsuit forced Thomas County schools to integrate, reshaping Boston’s education system and linking it with Thomasville by the 1970s.
Before settlers arrived, the Creek and Apalachee Indians hunted and lived here, using the area’s oak forests and moss‑draped landscapes for sustenance.
Boston hosts Georgia’s oldest candy company, Dillon Candy, which began sweet‑making in 1918 and still crafts treats today.
